about.title: About Me
about.intro: I'm a fullstack developer with 5 years of experience building web applications that make a difference. I've worked at marketing (Authorify, US), B2B e-commerce (Take), and fintech (Verzel) companies. It all started with games. I loved playing them and always wanted to understand how they were made, so I ended up studying Systems Analysis and Development and fell for programming and this whole world of technology. That curiosity to take things apart and see how they work turned into a passion for building complete solutions, from the backend to the final pixel.

about.philosophy: I believe good software is invisible: it loads fast, is intuitive, and accessible to everyone. Every line of code I write has a purpose — solving a real problem, not impressing with unnecessary complexity.
about.approach: My approach combines fullstack vision with attention to detail. I work with React on the frontend and Java/Python/NestJS on the backend, deploying to the cloud with AWS and Docker. Outside of code, I co-founded RP.js — a JavaScript community in Ribeirão Preto — and developed Ribeirão Noir, an investigative game launched at the Book Fair and validated by 3 PhD academics.

game.title: Fishing
game.description: A fishing game inside the portfolio. One screen, three minigames, nine fish.
game.howToPlay: Space does everything: it casts the line and plays each fish's minigame.

intro: Hey, you made it. This lake is odd: freshwater and saltwater fish show up here out of nowhere. Nobody explains it.
Go on, click a mark on the water and the boat sails itself. Once there, cast the line.
catch: You landed one! See, easy. Look, you can sell it right here with me, at the shore shop.
Big fish pay better. Rare ones, much better.
sale: That's it. Now buy a better line with the coins — the line is what lets you fish deeper.
And listen, there is a lot more fish than you have seen. A lot more. Take a look at the log.

world.clickHint: Click a mark to sail there
world.noSpot: Sail to a mark on the water
world.needLine: Your line is too short for this depth

instruction.track: Space when the marker crosses the zone.
instruction.hold: Hold space to rise. Keep the fish inside the band.
instruction.dodge: Space switches lane. Stay clean until the bar fills.

game.guaranteedModeHelp: Slower, but always lands the fish.

page.tagline: A small fishing game that runs in the browser. Three minigames, 24 Brazilian species and a lake to sail.
page.why1: I was hooked on fishing games. I recommend Dredge and Dave the Diver to everyone, and I hope you enjoy this little one here.
page.why2: It is silly and simple, and I know it may not be the most fun thing you play today. That is why how it was made comes right below.
page.how1: This game is completely vibe coded. I wrote a spec setting out the idea and saying it needed tests and had to be faithful to what I asked for.
page.how2: Each minigame engine is a pair, with pure logic in a tested file and a visual shell that only draws what the logic says. There are 179 tests, and the whole time we were trying not to grow the weight of loading the game.
page.how3: The images were generated with codex. The code and the image prompts were written by Claude Code, and I was approving or asking for improvements on what was being made. You can see all of it on my GitHub.
page.shotVenda: The bait shack on the bank, with the pier and the moored boat
page.shotNoite: The same lake at night, with lit windows on the far bank
page.shotMinigame: The rings minigame, with the world dimmed behind it
page.stack: Astro, Preact and TypeScript. No engine, no game dependency. The art is pixel art, generated and reviewed by hand, and the lake is CSS.
page.shotLoja: The bank shop open over the lake, with the catch to sell and the prices of the line and baits
